clue.text: Peer half-heartedly supporting church out of necessity

indicators.note: the word Peer loses one of the two letters at its heart, so it is only half there in the middle

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lord, not fully committed, backs the church only because he has no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Es of PEER, leaving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning by force of circumstance, unavoidably.

clue.text: Wind instrument, one joining piano in exercises

indicators.note: the pair of letters is placed inside the abbreviation for exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: one is joined by piano, set side by side

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A woodwind player joins the pianist during practice sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple tube blown to sound a note is one of the oldest wind instruments.

clue.text: Scottish dance about to be supported by the Spanish

parts.note: re means about or concerning
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.definitionFit: A lively folk dance of Scotland, danced in sets to fast music.

clue.text: Obvious, with OU intervening, transmission ended!

indicators.note: the inserted letters come between the parts of the word for obvious

parts.note: overt means open, plainly obvious
and joins, so it can stand for with

explanation.surface: A radio operator signs off, the Open University having butted in.
explanation.walkthrough: OU (the Open University) is given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio sign-off phrase announcing that a message is finished and no reply is expected.

clue.text: Decent participants in match as televised

indicators.note: the letters take part in the run of words that follows, hiding inside them

explanation.surface: The players in a broadcast match behave respectably.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent in the sense of pure and modest in conduct.

clue.text: Nothing from first bit of zinc aggregate returned

the word for aggregate is read backwards

parts.note: ore is mineral aggregate rock from which metal is mined

clue.text: Impartiality of energy standard

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
quality is a standard of excellence

explanation.surface: A judge's fairness is said to be a matter of energy and high standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating all equally is fairness, so being even-handed is impartiality.

clue.text: Think too much of a concern for cricket umpires?

definitions.meaning: to value someone or something more highly than deserved
umpires watch the rate at which overs are bowled

explanation.surface: Umpires fuss over something they may be overvaluing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; teams must bowl their overs at a set pace, the over rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate the merit of something is to overvalue it.

clue.text: Common person that is to be back in scheme

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit inside the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
be is the verb to be

explanation.surface: An ordinary person sees his part in the plan reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a commoner, not a patrician; hence an ordinary person.

clue.text: Judge with a Parisienne for thirty days

parts.note: une is the feminine French for a, as a Parisian woman would say

explanation.surface: A judge and a woman from Paris spend a month together.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'Thirty days hath September, April, June and November'.
explanation.definitionFit: A month with thirty days, as the old counting rhyme lists.

clue.text: Waste material spoiled smart place

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Rubbish has ruined a fashionable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal pieces collected for recycling are waste material.

clue.text: Specific rail-car put out

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A particular railway carriage has been taken out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'put' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular and specific are synonyms: relating to one definite thing.

clue.text: Mood displayed by a doctor having treated niece

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the letters of niece are worked on and changed, as a doctor treats a patient

explanation.surface: A doctor's bedside manner shows as he treats his niece.

clue.text: Follow the rules: quiet song followed by loud tune

indicators.note: the second pair of pieces comes after the first

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
f is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Musicians playing by the book: a soft song, then a loud tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To act honestly and within the rules of a game is to behave fairly.

clue.text: Notes my accepting unemployment benefit returned

indicators.note: the word my takes the reversed letters inside it

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Banknotes from the dole come back to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like money beside the benefit, but it means musical notes.

clue.text: Point about sparkling wine: not much good now?

indicators.note: the letters for point go around the wine

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont, Italy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bottle of fizz has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone or something too old to be effective any more.

clue.text: Article on complex maths leads to complaint

indicators.note: the article is put on, in front of, what follows

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so these letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: An essay on difficult maths brings on an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and this is a breathing disorder.

clue.text: Arrangement of music — key of A, not C, in my opinion

parts.note: the letter C is the one left out of the mix

explanation.walkthrough: Letters of MUSIC KEY OF A, less C, rearranged give the phrase.

clue.text: Yank throttling husband is ruffian

parts.note: to yank is to tug

explanation.surface: An American strangling her husband is a brute.

clue.text: Didn't stand around waiting initially for strike

indicators.note: the phrase for not standing goes round the initial letter

parts.note: one who didn't stand sat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of waiting is taken

explanation.surface: Workers sat about waiting for a strike to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit sharply, as at a fly, is to strike.

clue.text: Article caught like a fish? That's ingenious

indicators.note: the article is caught inside, held as in a trap

parts.note: a fish is taken in a net, so the question hints at the net
a is the indefinite article

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'caught like a fish' as one idea (netted); split it into the container signal and the net itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an exclamation of approval for a clever or ingenious idea.

clue.text: TV programme possibly caps tucking into food

clue.text: Regret backing old currency

indicators.note: the word for regret is put into reverse

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.definitionFit: The single currency of much of the European Union.

clue.text: Silver reflected faint source of illumination
